As Apple Computer (AAPL) Shares Declined, Shareholder Berkshire Asset Management Has Upped Stake; Exxon Mobil (XOM) Shareholder Univest Of Pennsylvania Has Lowered Stake as Market Valuation Declined
May 10, 2018 - By Russell Anderson
Berkshire Asset Management Llc increased its stake in Apple Computer (AAPL) by 39.42% based on its latest 2017Q4 regulatory filing with the SEC. Berkshire Asset Management Llc bought 7,086 shares as the company’s stock declined 3.81% with the market. The hedge fund held 25,060 shares of the computer manufacturing company at the end of 2017Q4, valued at $4.24 million, up from 17,974 at the end of the previous reported quarter. Berkshire Asset Management Llc who had been investing in Apple Computer for a number of months, seems to be bullish on the $926.19 billion market cap company. The stock increased 0.57% or $1.0762 during the last trading session, reaching $188.4362. About 7.19 million shares traded. Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL) has risen 19.49% since May 10, 2017 and is uptrending. It has outperformed by 7.94% the S&P500.
Univest Corp Of Pennsylvania decreased its stake in Exxon Mobil Corp (XOM) by 28.93% based on its latest 2017Q4 regulatory filing with the SEC. Univest Corp Of Pennsylvania sold 6,248 shares as the company’s stock declined 12.23% with the market. The institutional investor held 15,351 shares of the integrated oil company at the end of 2017Q4, valued at $1.28M, down from 21,599 at the end of the previous reported quarter. Univest Corp Of Pennsylvania who had been investing in Exxon Mobil Corp for a number of months, seems to be less bullish one the $342.77B market cap company. The stock increased 1.29% or $1.03 during the last trading session, reaching $80.96. About 4.10M shares traded. Exxon Mobil Corporation (NYSE:XOM) has declined 9.29% since May 10, 2017 and is downtrending. It has underperformed by 20.84% the S&P500.
